display: Former cabin crew trainer at a big Gulf airline college for fourteen years, based in Dubai.

signals.text: I'm open to new work in crew training, candidate assessment or onboarding, and I'd like to find where my experience fits.
I'd like someone to ask me why 'what does the candidate do when they don't know the answer?' predicts emergency performance better than a grooming score.
I keep rewriting my interview assessment sheets with scenario questions and a column for observed behaviour under mild stress, and I want that work to be used by someone.
I have every weekday free since the July restructuring and I miss running sessions and debriefs.
I want to test my redesigned assessment sheet on real candidates and see whether it spots calm people better than confident talkers.
My son is applying to UK universities (Manchester, Leeds, Edinburgh, UCL as a long shot) and I'd like to hear from parents or alumni who have been through it.
I'm trying to help my son write a personal statement that tells his real story of moving countries and having an accent.
I'm staying in Dubai until my son's university results arrive in spring, so I need work here and not a relocation.
My Dubai residence visa is tied to my old employer and runs out on 30 November. I need new sponsorship or another legal arrangement.
Savings are thinning and I can't afford a long gap in income. I'm weighing whether to sell my car.
The restructuring hurt, and I miss being 'the trainer'. I'm still working out who I am without that role.

offers.text: Fourteen years of cabin crew training at a major Gulf airline college: service sequences, grooming, safety and emergency drills, and interview assessment.
Six years of flying as cabin crew, so I understand the job from both the trainer's side and the crew's side.
A binder of interview assessment sheets, rubrics, role-play scenarios and rewritten scoring guides that I can adapt for airline, hospitality or service-sector hiring.
I can design and run a candidate assessment day, with scenario role-plays and structured observation of behaviour under mild stress.
I can coach nervous people into confident, calm performers, whether for interviews, customer-facing roles or high-pressure service.
I can build or review training curricula for service and safety culture, and train other trainers.
I know many people in the Dubai aviation world: former trainees now senior crew, instructors and recruiters. I can introduce people when there's a good fit.
I'm free on weekdays for consulting, freelance training or a part-time project.
I can lead a dawn run in the desert near Al Qudra with a friendly group, and I bring dates and coffee.

catchers.hypo: We're a small airline or charter operator and our crew interviews keep hiring people who impress on the day but struggle under pressure. Could someone review our assessment process?
catchers.can: Audit their interview process and offer a redesigned scoring sheet with scenario questions and observed-behaviour criteria, as a paid consulting job.
catchers.confirm: Is the role about assessing or training cabin crew, or similar customer-facing safety-critical staff, rather than only recruiting corporate or office staff?

catchers.hypo: I run a hospitality or airport-services company in the UAE and need someone to build a training programme for new front-line staff.
catchers.can: Design and deliver a training curriculum covering service standards, grooming, handling stress and basic emergency procedures.
catchers.confirm: Does the work need a trainer with real experience of high-stakes service environments, and can it be done in Dubai on weekdays?

catchers.hypo: I'm a nervous candidate with an airline cabin crew interview in three weeks. Do you coach people for it?
catchers.can: Run mock interviews and role-plays with feedback, drawing on fourteen years of assessing real candidates.
catchers.confirm: Is the person applying to a cabin crew or comparable customer-facing airline role?

catchers.hypo: I'm the HR lead at a training academy or aviation company and need an experienced trainer who can sponsor or help us onboard on a visa. Do you know someone who'd fit?
catchers.can: Consider a full-time or part-time training role. Sponsorship terms would be discussed once there is real interest.
catchers.confirm: Does the role include a legal route to residency in the UAE, and is it with an employer that does not undercut crew training standards?

catchers.hypo: Our son is applying from the Gulf to UK universities and he's worried about being the kid with the accent. Has anyone you know been through this?
catchers.can: Share what has worked in helping my own seventeen-year-old write a personal statement about moving countries, and compare notes on the application process.
catchers.confirm: Is the student applying from a family based in the Gulf to UK universities this cycle, and does the parent want peer advice, not paid admissions consulting?

catchers.hypo: I'm a former crew member who was recently laid off and I feel lost without the job. How did people around you cope?
catchers.can: Offer a listening ear, share how trainer-to-next-chapter transitions can work, and introduce them to former trainees and recruiters in aviation.
catchers.confirm: Is the person from an aviation or service background looking for support or networking, rather than urgent financial or legal help?

catchers.hypo: I'm a researcher or startup founder working on how to predict who performs well under stress. Would you share what you've seen in 14 years of assessments?
catchers.can: Explain why the 'what do you do when you don't know the answer' column predicted emergency performance, and discuss testing the rubric on real candidates.
catchers.confirm: Is the work about assessing observed behaviour under pressure, and would it let me share non-confidential rubric ideas without disclosing named candidate data?

catchers.hypo: My friend, a former airline trainee, now a senior crew member, is looking for a mentor to prepare her for a purser or instructor promotion board.
catchers.can: Coach her directly, or connect her with former trainees who have recently made the same step, since several now work as pursers and long-haul crew.
catchers.confirm: Is the person currently flying or recently flew as cabin crew and aiming for a senior or instructor role?

catchers.hypo: I've heard you work with a college or a recruiter whose standards for crew selection are dropping. Can you help us bring them back?
catchers.can: Introduce them to Hannah, a former colleague still at the training college, or to other instructors who care about standards, and advise on what to restore.
catchers.confirm: Is the organisation trying to raise its selection and training standards rather than cut cost or loosen requirements?

catchers.hypo: I'm a Dubai running group organiser. Would you help new runners get started in the desert at dawn?
catchers.can: Welcome new people into a friendly 5:15 a.m. group near Al Qudra with six regulars.
catchers.confirm: Is the person comfortable with a very early weekend start and a social, non-competitive pace?

forbids.text: I won't work for a competitor that has undercut the standards of my old team's training.
I'm not leaving Dubai before my son's university results come out in spring.
I keep weekends for family and the desert.
I can't take a long gap without income or a role that leaves me without a legal route to stay.
I won't share my family's private details, such as my son's documents, health or finances.

projects.name: Behaviour-under-stress assessment sheet
projects.text: A redesigned interview assessment with scenario questions and an observed-behaviour-under-mild-stress column, including the 'what do you do when you don't know the answer?' item. It needs real candidates and a home.
roles_needed: airline or hospitality recruiter willing to pilot it
assessment or HR researcher to help validate it
designer to format it into a usable toolkit

policy.t1: When there's a real lead, I'll share that I'm available on weekdays, that I keep rewriting my interview assessment sheets, that my son is applying to UK universities, and how my rubrics work.
policy.t2: Once trust and the other party's identity are clear, I'll share my visa timeline and the need for sponsorship, my financial pressure and how the restructuring affected me.
policy.never: My bank details, my son's passport and medical details, and anything about who in my family or running group doesn't yet know about my job loss.
